subject: Unexpected token spike — request for raw metering export and EU VAT treatment
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@auroraai.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: finance@auroraai.com
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 08:12:00 +0100
Subject: Large spike on Sep 30 invoice — raw logs + VAT question

Vanessa,

We noticed a very large token spike on the Sep 30 invoice (invoice attached) that doesn't line up with our telemetry. Summary: Redwood billed ~3.4M tokens for 2026-09-30 for our integration; our internal logs show ~400k tokens for the same period.

I've attached a small sample export (aurora_usage_sample_20260930.csv) showing the request_ids and timestamps. Can you:
- Provide the raw per-request metering export for 2026-09-30 (including request_id, model, token_in, token_out, route, ingest_window)
- Explain whether any tokenizer or backend model changes happened on your side that day
- Confirm how credits/refunds would be handled (we're pausing payment on the contested invoice until cleared)
- Clarify VAT treatment — Aurora AI is an Irish entity (EU VAT reverse-charge should apply). Will the adjustment/credit be issued net of VAT?

We need the raw logs for our audit team (we can upload to your shared Drive link if you prefer). This is time-sensitive as our finance team is holding the payment.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Finance — Aurora AI
liam.oconnor@auroraai.com
+353 1 555 0942

Attachments: aurora_usage_sample_20260930.csv, original_invoice_202609.pdf
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@auroraai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Large spike on Sep 30 invoice — raw logs + VAT question

Hi Liam — thanks for the heads up and for the sample. I've looped in Ben from Finance and Marissa from Accounts for the contract side.

Quick plan:
1) Ben will run a preliminary reconciliation and look for duplicate request_ids/double-counting tied to streaming/session routing.
2) We will produce a raw metering export (CSV) for the full 2026-09-30 day with the fields you requested. I'll share a secure Drive link once the export is ready (ETA 48 hours).
3) To reduce disruption on your end, we can provisionally place the invoice on hold and apply a provisional credit for the disputed portion while we investigate.

A couple of clarifying Qs:
- Do you want the export with full payload hashes/redactions, or is request_id + model + token counts sufficient for your audit team?
- Please confirm the specific company VAT number so we can prepare the credit note correctly.

We aim to resolve this quickly — Ben, can you prioritize the raw log export check? Marissa, I'll need a quick note on contract terms if we need to issue an invoice adjustment/credit note.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Manager — Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Office: +1 415 682 2090

On Mon, Oct 5, 2026 at 08:12 AM Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@auroraai.com> wrote:
> Vanessa,
>
> We noticed a very large token spike on the Sep 30 invoice... (sample attached)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@auroraai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Large spike on Sep 30 invoice — preliminary findings

Liam / Vanessa,

I pulled a quick reconciliation against our metering pipeline. High level: there was a configuration change that day tied to a streaming proxy used by a small group of customers. The proxy introduced a replication header for some streaming sessions which, under a particular routing path, caused the same conversational prefix to be submitted twice to Redwood's batching layer for ~2.95M tokens.

What I can provide now (attached sooner rather than later):
- Full per-request CSV for 2026-09-30 (request_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, route, ingestion_window, replication_flag)
- A short traceback showing request_ids that were deduplicated vs. those double-queued

Proposed remediation steps:
1) Apply a one-time usage credit for duplicated tokens. From our counts, duplicated tokens ~2,950,412.
2) Pricing reference: Aurora's rate for the model in question is $0.00040 / token_out. Proposed credit = 2,950,412 * $0.00040 = $1,180.1648 (rounding on invoice will be $1,180.16).
3) VAT: Since Aurora is an EU entity with reverse-charge, we will issue the credit note net of VAT (no VAT charged on the credit). Please confirm Aurora's VAT number and we will generate a corrected invoice/credit.

I will upload the CSV to the secure Drive link Vanessa will share. If you prefer to receive the logs via SFTP, we can arrange that — let us know.

Next steps: Vanessa to confirm contract/credit workflow; Liam to confirm VAT number and acceptance of the proposed credit. Once accepted, Marissa will issue the credit note and we will apply it to the outstanding invoice; expected account posting within 3 business days after sign-off.

Ben Carter
Billing Lead — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Attachments to follow: redwood_metering_20260930_full.csv, duplication_traceback.txt
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@auroraai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: finance@auroraai.com
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 09:14:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Large spike on Sep 30 invoice — acceptance and VAT confirmation

Ben / Vanessa — thanks for the quick look and the proposed remediation. Aurora confirms our VAT number: IE3524897V. We agree with the proposed credit calculation and the explanation (replicated streaming submissions). A few practical Qs before you issue the credit note:
- Please send the corrected invoice/credit note indicating net amount and a note: "Reverse-charge applies — VAT to be accounted for by the customer under Article 194 of the VAT Directive."
- Timing: we need the corrected invoice to clear our AP queue by Oct 12 so we can close this month without block.
- Can you confirm the corrected invoice will reference original_invoice_202609.pdf so our ledgers match?

If you can share the redwood_metering_20260930_full.csv to our secure Drive link, that will be sufficient for our auditors. Once we receive the credit note we will release the payment hold on the non-disputed remainder of the invoice.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Finance — Aurora AI
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@auroraai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Large spike on Sep 30 invoice — next steps and links

Liam — confirmed.

Summary of agreed next steps:
- Ben has uploaded redwood_metering_20260930_full.csv and duplication_traceback.txt to the Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.example.com/aurora/raw-metering-logs (files are available now).
- Marissa will prepare a credit note referencing original_invoice_202609.pdf for $1,180.16 (net of VAT) with the reverse-charge language requested. You should receive the credit note and adjusted invoice by EOD Oct 10 UTC; posting to our ledger within 1–2 business days thereafter.
- We will mark the invoice as "under investigation" in our billing system so collections are paused for the disputed amount. The remaining undisputed balance will not be held up.

If anything changes on your side please flag immediately — otherwise we'll proceed as above. Thanks for the clear sample export which made the triage straightforward.

Best regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Manager — Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: soc2-audit-redacted.pdf
